chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Kirby's early life and his charm
summary: Liner-note descriptions of Kirby as a charmer; little is known of his youth.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: From the line of notes from Columbia records, John Kirby, The Boss of The Bass, gets an image of him as maybe an impulsive kind of a person and a great

S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC.
WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
charmer. I think that word was used. In fact there's a quote, where is it, from Red Allen, 'he charmed the birds down from the trees'.

You know, Red Allen probably knew Kirby for a long time, you know. Although we were married there was a lot of things about Kirby that I didn't know because our being separated quite a bit. And Kirby had quite a long history of successes, you know, as a musician long before I ever met him. So I really don't know that much about his early life.
He didn't talk too much about his early life, because apparently not too much is known about it other than the fact that he was an orphan and he was raised by adoptive parents in Baltimore.

Yeah, that's just about all I ever knew about him too. We only talked about, you know, what we were doing, music and stuff like that. There wasn't, I don't suppose he wanted to talk about his past. He didn't have any family that I knew about. But he knew about my family because we had gone to Homestead several times and he met my mother. And we went to Homestead to try and get my son to come and live with me and we

had to go back a couple of times. But I never knew too much about Kurby's family. He and Benny Carter and Buster Bailey seemed to be very, very close friends. And I suppose if anybody knew anything about him it would have been those two people. I don't think he was inclined to talk about himself that much.
